definition: An epithelial cell that is part of the epithelium of the palatine tonsil, a mucosa-associated lymphoid organ of the oropharynx. The palatine tonsil epithelium encompasses two co-existing compartments: a surface stratified squamous epithelium continuous with the oral mucosa, and a specialised reticulated crypt epithelium characterised by a loosely organised structure, incomplete basement membrane, and infiltration by lymphoid cells (PMID:34430822; PMID:30955493). Both compartments express keratins contributing to mechanical integrity (PMID:41518352). This subset is transcriptomically distinguished by elevated VEGFA mRNA expression; the biological basis of this marker is not yet characterised.

logical_axioms.notes: Cells reside in the epithelial layer of the tonsil, spanning both surface stratified squamous and reticulated crypt compartments. UBERON:0013696 (tonsil epithelium) is more precise than the whole organ (UBERON:0002373) and is transitive to it via the part_of chain.

Tonsil epithelium participates in antigen transport and barrier functions that are part of the broader mucosal immune response (PMID:33995367; PMID:36693202). The epithelial cell carries out part of this process; the full immune response involves additional cell types.

synonyms.value: VEGFA-positive epithelial cell of the palatine tonsil

justification: An exhaustive search of OLS4 CL revealed no existing term for any epithelial cell of the palatine tonsil, the tonsil crypt, or the tonsil surface epithelium. CL:0000066 (epithelial cell) is the most specific valid broad parent. CL:0000240 (stratified squamous epithelial cell) was rejected because the atlas annotation encompasses the reticulated crypt epithelium, which is not squamous and lacks an intact basement membrane. The atlas subset is defined transcriptomically by elevated VEGFA mRNA in the Azimuth human_tonsil_v2 reference (King et al., 2021); direct in situ validation of VEGFA protein in tonsil epithelium is not available in the traversed literature. VEGFA is a secreted growth factor characterised at transcript level only in this atlas context: no `has plasma membrane part` axiom is warranted, and an `expresses` axiom for VEGFA is flagged as provisional pending protein-level confirmation. The strongest anchors for ontological placement are (1) epithelial cell identity, (2) location in tonsil epithelium (UBERON:0013696), and (3) functional participation in mucosal immune defence. A future CL editor may wish to add two child terms: one for surface stratified squamous epithelial cell of the palatine tonsil (child of CL:0000240) and one for reticulated crypt epithelial cell of the palatine tonsil (child of CL:0000066), with the VEGFA-positive subset represented as a post-compositional expression qualifier once those parents exist.

**Additional notes or concerns**
This term is needed to represent epithelial cells of the human palatine tonsil identified in the Azimuth human_tonsil_v2 single-cell reference atlas (King et al., Science Immunology, 2021; PMID:34623901; DOI:10.1126/sciimmunol.abh3768). No existing CL term covers this anatomical context: searches for tonsil epithelial cell, reticulated epithelial cell, crypt epithelial cell, lymphoepithelial cell, oral epithelial cell, and pharyngeal epithelial cell all returned no results.

The atlas annotation label is "VEGFA+" (elevated VEGFA mRNA by scRNA-seq), but VEGFA is a broadly expressed secreted growth factor, not a cell-type-specific surface marker. No axiom asserting `has plasma membrane part` or `expresses` VEGFA is proposed at this stage; these should await protein-level validation in the tonsil compartment specifically.

The tonsil epithelium spans two structurally distinct compartments (Arambula et al., 2021; Roberts et al., 2019; Crowell et al., 2025), and this term intentionally covers both. A CL editor may wish to add two future child terms:
- surface stratified squamous epithelial cell of the palatine tonsil (child of CL:0000240)
- reticulated crypt epithelial cell of the palatine tonsil (child of CL:0000066)

- subClassOf 'part of' some 'tonsil epithelium' (UBERON:0013696) [BFO:0000050]
- subClassOf 'capable of part of' some 'mucosal immune response' (GO:0002385) [RO:0002216]
